about.title: El Cerrito Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and the paperwork and legal deadlines that follow are often the last thing a grieving family wants to face. El Cerrito recorded 4 traffic deaths in the most recent final crash year, alongside 52 injury collisions on corridors like San Pablo Avenue, I-80, Route 123, and Potrero Avenue. Many of these crashes cluster on Wednesday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m., a window when commuter traffic through Contra Costa County tends to be heaviest. If your family has lost a loved one in a crash anywhere in El Cerrito, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who focuses on wrongful death matters. The attorney can walk you through California's rules on who may file, what losses can be claimed, and how much time you have left before a deadline passes. You focus on your family; let someone else handle the legal calendar.

whyChoose.title: Why El Cerrito Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Can Be Confusing
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents or heirs. An independent attorney can help sort out who in your family qualifies to file.

items.title: The Clock Starts Running Immediately
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks considerably if a government entity, such as a public road agency, may be involved. Waiting to seek guidance can cost your family options.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs and lost financial support, as well as compensation for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney can help make sure none of these losses are overlooked.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action pursued by the family, distinct from any criminal charges the driver may face. The two proceedings run independently, and a civil claim can move forward regardless of the criminal outcome.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing, and an attorney can review your family's specific situation to clarify who qualifies.

items.question: My family member died in a crash near San Pablo Avenue involving a city street. Does that change our deadline?
items.answer: It might. Claims involving a government entity, such as a city or county road authority, often carry a much shorter filing deadline than the standard two years. Because El Cerrito's higher-volume corridors include public roadways, it's worth having an attorney review the crash location and circumstances quickly.

items.question: What costs can my family recover through a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and compensation for the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can help evaluate which losses apply to your family's circumstances.
